works.name: ADAPT for Science: A Multi-Agent System for Self-Evolving Scientific Optimization
works.summary: Combines retrieval of historical scientific designs, evolving start-selection strategies, and optimizer-program evolution under physical constraints. The authors evaluate gravitational-wave detector designs on eight held-out topologies using a differentiable simulator and matched scientific evaluation budgets. Results support optimization within this setting; transfer beyond simulation and dependence on historical-library coverage remain open.

works.name: GeoAgent: Contract-Constrained LLM Agents for Seismic Data Processing
works.summary: Connects seismic-processing tools through a fixed nine-stage graph, with explicit contracts for artifacts, input resolution, parameter ownership, and output validation. Deterministic geometry checks address failures that prompting alone did not prevent. Evidence comes from engineering measurements on one dataset and model family; adaptive planning, migration quality, and broader controlled comparisons remain unestablished.

works.name: RIDAR: Safeguarding Research Integrity in Autonomous Research Agents via Automated Detection and Runtime Intervention
works.summary: Audits research trajectories with separate Analyzer and Verifier agents, then tests runtime feedback against matched unassisted runs. Its taxonomy covers 14 integrity violations. Reported findings depend on LLM judgments and mathematics/ML tasks; testing files and extra resources remain accessible deliberately, so detected violation rates should not be generalized to environments enforcing those boundaries.

works.name: Astro2Method
works.summary: Tests machine-learning method selection with 500 expert-reviewed binary questions derived from 346 astronomy papers. Questions distinguish complete from partial methodological explanations. Historical retrieval and additional agent reasoning do not consistently improve accuracy; web-search gains concentrate on finding the source papers. This measures retrospective method judgments, not executing alternative methods or establishing prospective astronomical discoveries.

works.name: ExpEvolve: Structuring and Reusing Experience for Open-Ended Discovery
works.summary: Extracts interpretable idea factors from archived programs whose score differences remain unexplained, then uses bandit-selected edits and plateau-triggered exploration to guide program evolution. Evaluations cover eleven mathematical tasks and six machine-learning engineering tasks. Reported gains concern bounded executable objectives; the theoretical benefits require stated assumptions, and transfer to expensive scientific verification remains untested.

works.name: GAV: A scientific experimentation environment for PDE agents
works.summary: Learns continuous reference solutions and constructs matching PDE problems through manufactured solutions, giving coding agents numerical feedback without solving every new reference problem. Evaluations cover Navier–Stokes and Vlasov–Poisson-type tasks and adaptations of existing PDE agents. Its reliability analysis assumes controlled distribution mismatch and independent evaluation data; success on generated problems does not establish accuracy across arbitrary physical regimes.

works.name: Recursive Flint
works.summary: An open-weight mixture-of-experts coding model built with Recursive’s Eureka Machine and a human team. The model card specifies 39.8B total parameters and approximately 2.5B active per token, including the output head. Included as a concrete automated-research output and reusable coding component; released weights and inference code do not independently validate the development process or reported performance.

works.name: Automating ML for Science: Can Frontier Agents Climb Scientific Hills in the Wild?
works.summary: Studies frontier coding agents improving scientific ML baselines in Agent4Sci, separating optimization, held-out evaluation, and trajectory auditing. Default gains are largely engineering-driven; targeted research skills produce more varied interventions. The study distinguishes metric improvement from scientific insight, with limitations from run variance, imperfect audits, task-specific skills, and the absence of a human-researcher baseline.

works.name: Autonomous adaptive spectral analysis with an LLM agent for self-driving laboratories
works.summary: Uses an LLM to inspect spectra and diagnostics, adjust predefined fitting parameters within bounded retries, or abstain, while deterministic code calculates the physical quantity. On 203 archived film spectra, it retains 183 baseline values, recovers 16 failed analyses, and abstains on four. This retrospective, single-campaign study does not test live laboratory control or detection of physically incorrect results that pass numerical checks.

works.name: Bayesian Model Discovery with Language Models: Closing the Loop between Hypotheses and Experiments
works.summary: Combines LLM-proposed functional forms with numerical parameter fitting, evidence-weighted predictions, and experiment selection by joint information gain over models and parameters. Four benchmarks compare predictive error and structural recovery, with ablations of numerical feedback. Results depend on the candidate pool, priors, and observation model; containing the true law as a special case is explicitly distinguished from recovering its exact form.

works.name: Magnolia: A Persistent-Memory Agent Framework for Computational Chemistry
works.summary: Combines computational chemistry tools with session records, confirmed project knowledge, and human-reviewed rules reused across projects. Four case studies and controlled replays of four internal tasks examine the contribution of retained context. The authors explicitly position it as supervised research assistance; campaign-wide memory benefits remain unisolated, and complete docking records include unreleased collaborator results.

works.name: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
works.summary: Extracts atomic claims from published cancer-registry studies, executes reproduction analyses, and tests alternative analytical choices through agent-generated perturbations. SEER-Repro supplies the evaluation setting. The authors distinguish reproducing reported findings from assessing their sensitivity; flagged alternatives require expert review, and report-based grading does not independently verify the complete analysis code.

works.name: DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses
works.summary: Develops hypothesis trees through multi-agent search, compiles selected investigations into Harbor tasks, and improves subsequent research through contribution-weighted model training and workflow replay. DFM-Bench assesses proposals and their development. Reported gains concern hypothesis quality and retrospective literature correspondence; these measures do not establish independently validated discoveries or causal influence on later publications.

works.name: PhysClosureBench
works.summary: Provides 50 physics research tasks with specified goals and constraints. A 20-criterion score measures local accomplishments, while a separate closure assessment tests whether essential evidence and applicability conditions resolve the research question. Model-based grading includes a selected human consistency check; high partial scores are not equivalent to complete scientific closure.

works.name: SciPIvot
works.summary: Tests scientific judgment through 248 decisions drawn from human corrections across 26 research projects. Models choose between an original agent plan and a human-corrected alternative, with or without the prior project record. This evaluates recognition of selected corrective decisions, not plan generation, research execution, or the prevalence of failures across scientific work.

works.name: The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery
works.summary: Coordinates coding agents through task drafting, ideas, sandboxed experiments, baselines, ablations, analysis, and manuscript writing. A meta-controller enforces stage-specific rubrics. The paper reports computational discovery studies and an ALIFE 2026 paper produced in a co-scientist setting; that human collaboration should be distinguished from its separate autonomous evaluations.

works.name: Can AI Scientists Coordinate at Runtime?
works.summary: Adds runtime agent selection, scoped work contracts, and artifact-based verification to existing scientist frameworks. A single-seed exploratory study compares cumulative coordination variants under host-calibrated budgets. Runtime selection gives the strongest observed means, while additional contracts and verification can reduce scores, exposing tradeoffs that larger replicated evaluations should investigate.

works.name: Denario Project: Deep Knowledge Artificial Intelligence Agents for Scientific Discovery
works.summary: Provides modular agents for ideation, literature checking, planning, code execution, plotting, writing, and reviewing, using Cmbagent for analysis. Demonstrations span multiple scientific disciplines and include domain-expert reviews of generated drafts. The authors position it as a research assistant, with case-study quality and limitations requiring inspection of each output.

works.name: Agentic AI–Physicist Collaboration in Experimental Particle Physics: A Proof-of-Concept Measurement with LEP Open Data
works.summary: Demonstrates an agent-assisted thrust measurement from archived ALEPH collision data, including code execution, unfolding, uncertainty propagation, and manuscript drafting. Physicists supply prior analyses and context, define acceptance criteria, inspect results, and approve major decisions. The published contribution is a supervised analysis demonstration using a known observable, not an autonomous discovery or a controlled estimate of productivity gains.

works.name: ScientistTwo: Pioneering the Human Knowledge Frontier with Autonomous AI
works.summary: Starts from a research problem, establishes baselines, proposes hypotheses, runs experiments and ablations, and iterates through simulated reviews. Evaluation includes publication-derived machine-learning tasks, integrity audits, automated reviewers, and a human study of generated papers. These complementary author-reported assessments remain bounded by the selected tasks; simulated acceptance is distinct from actual venue acceptance.

works.name: ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents
works.summary: Turns researcher requests, feedback, and execution traces into learning tasks and evaluation rubrics. An inner loop adapts the agent harness while an outer loop trains the model under the improved harness. Case studies cover four scientific task families; they demonstrate the proposed learning workflow rather than universal autonomous discovery.

works.name: IdeaForecastBench
works.summary: Evaluates whether ideas proposed from literature available before a cutoff correspond to later publications. It contains 624 rolling episodes across 52 topics, generates up to five ranked ideas, and reports separate judge results. This measures research forecasting under a retrospective protocol; broad or generic predictions and judge sensitivity complicate interpretation as precise scientific anticipation.

works.name: ResearchStudio
works.summary: Microsoft's research skill collection includes Idea for developing literature-grounded research proposals and Reel for turning completed papers into posters, narrated videos, blogs, and interactive presentations. The code exposes editable workflows for coding agents. Its two modules support different stages of research and communication; their presence does not establish an autonomous experimental discovery pipeline.

works.name: Recursive Eureka Machine
works.summary: Recursive describes an automated research loop that proposes ideas, implements experiments, checks results, and carries useful context across parallel investigations. Public examples include training and GPU-kernel optimization; its later Flint model provides a released development outcome. Available research artifacts support inspection of selected outputs, but do not establish access to the complete research framework or independently verified autonomy.

works.name: SoundnessBench: Can Your AI Scientist Really Tell Good Research Ideas from Bad Ones?
works.summary: Examines whether language models can assess methodological soundness before experiments are run. Results-masked proposals receive reviewer-derived proxy labels and separate expert judgments on a subset. Standard prompts favor approval, while aggressive prompts trade false approvals for false rejections. The study concerns proposal-stage judgment; its labels do not establish experimental truth or general research quality.

works.name: ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence
works.summary: Maintains explicit evidence chains from literature and experiments to manuscript claims, with audits for score reproduction, specification violations, references, and method-code agreement. The authors compare generated papers across research tasks and report improved integrity. These are task-specific audits, so the title's human-level claim should not be generalized to all research.

works.name: Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist
works.summary: Uses specialized agents to generate, criticize, rank, and evolve hypotheses through tournaments, with scientists setting goals and steering exploration. The Nature paper includes biomedical applications and laboratory validation of selected hypotheses. The system supports scientific reasoning; experimental validation remains a distinct process rather than an automatically closed physical loop.

works.name: Empirical Research Assistance: An AI system to help scientists write expert-level empirical software
works.summary: Uses language-model code mutations and tree search to improve a specified empirical quality metric, incorporating research ideas from external sources. The Nature paper evaluates diverse scientific software tasks, including bioinformatics and forecasting. Its strength is experimentally scored implementation search; results depend on the supplied objectives, evaluation data, and task design.

works.name: Robin: A multi-agent system for automating scientific discovery
works.summary: Combines literature agents and data-analysis agents in an iterative hypothesis, experiment, and interpretation cycle. The Nature study reports in-vitro evidence for candidate interventions affecting retinal-cell phagocytosis. Human researchers perform the physical experiments, and these preclinical findings do not establish treatment effectiveness in patients.

works.name: PaperOrchestra
works.summary: Transforms research ideas, experimental records, and formatting requirements into LaTeX manuscripts through specialized planning, literature, plotting, writing, and refinement agents. The official Google Research repository accompanies the paper and evaluation resources. It addresses synthesis of existing research materials; manuscript quality ratings do not verify that the underlying experiments or scientific conclusions are correct.

works.name: Towards end-to-end automation of AI research
works.summary: Integrates the AI Scientist lineage into a journal study of template-based and template-free research workflows, including idea generation, experiments, writing, and reviewing. A generated manuscript passed an initial workshop review round. This peer-reviewed system paper should be distinguished from the separate question of whether generated findings are independently replicated.

works.name: RINoBench
works.summary: Tests research-idea novelty judgments with 1,381 expert-derived ideas and nine metrics covering numerical novelty ratings and written justifications. The authors find that human-like explanations can coexist with inaccurate novelty judgments. This is useful for evaluating critic or reviewer agents, while novelty-rating agreement remains distinct from feasibility, empirical correctness, and discovery value.

works.name: EvoScientist: Towards Multi-Agent Evolving AI Scientists for End-to-End Scientific Discovery
works.summary: Separates research, engineering, and evolution-management roles, storing both ideation history and experiment lessons in persistent memory. The October 2026 revision reports gains in idea assessment and code-execution success. These evaluations support reuse of research experience, while broader discovery quality still requires inspection beyond successful code execution.

works.name: MOOSE-Star: Unlocking Tractable Training for Scientific Discovery by Breaking the Complexity Barrier
works.summary: Trains hypothesis generation through decomposed discovery subtasks, motivation-guided hierarchical retrieval, and bounded composition. It releases TOMATO-Star and studies scaling with training data and inference budget. The claimed complexity reduction depends on the paper's assumptions and best-case analysis; benchmark scaling is distinct from prospective experimental validation.

works.name: AutoIllustrate
works.summary: Converts a method description into an editable draw.io diagram, then optionally applies an image-generation restyling pass. The public command-line workflow includes figure generation and visual auditing and was used with Agentic Scientist. Retaining the vector source supports manual correction, but generated visual polish should not be taken as evidence of methodological fidelity.

works.name: Autonomous Research Agents: A Survey of AI Scientists and the Verification Gap
works.summary: Examines computational research agents through autonomy, evaluation, released artifacts, human intervention, novelty checks, and result-selection disclosure. Its coded corpus distinguishes runnable code from evidence that supports scientific claims. The conclusions are bounded by the screened AI/ML systems and coding rules, rather than a census of all scientific domains.

works.name: OpenResearch
works.summary: A local research workspace and harness from alphaXiv that connects coding agents to literature discovery, experiment execution, and artifact inspection. It records experiments in a local database and supports multiple compute backends. The repository documents a usable product; these capabilities are project claims rather than an independently established discovery benchmark.

works.name: PaperBanana
works.summary: Uses retrieval, planning, styling, visualization, and critique agents to generate academic diagrams and plots from scientific content. Its repository includes execution interfaces and a benchmark of reference illustrations. It is a useful study of iterative visual communication, with semantic accuracy and faithful representation of experimental data still requiring inspection beyond aesthetic judgments.

works.name: AInsteinBench
works.summary: Evaluates scientific software development using tasks derived from maintainer pull requests across six research codebases. Executable tests assess changes in domains including chemistry, molecular dynamics, and numerical relativity. This measures repository-level implementation and verification under specified tests; it does not assess autonomous hypothesis selection or establish correctness beyond the tested behavior.

works.name: FrontierScience
works.summary: Assesses expert-level physics, chemistry, and biology reasoning using Olympiad and Research splits. The released gold sets contain 100 short-answer questions and 60 research subtasks, with model grading against answers or rubrics. These constrained, expert-authored tasks probe scientific reasoning; the creators explicitly distinguish them from the broader work of producing new discoveries.

works.name: Kosmos: An AI Scientist for Autonomous Discovery
works.summary: Uses a structured world model to coordinate repeated literature search and data-analysis trajectories from an objective and dataset. Reports link claims to code or literature, and the paper presents seven discovery case studies with external scientist assessments. Human-equivalent time estimates are collaborator judgments rather than controlled productivity measurements.

works.name: A Survey of AI Scientists
works.summary: Synthesizes AI-scientist systems through six stages covering literature, ideas, preparation, execution, writing, and paper generation. The revised survey traces the shift from individual components to integrated workflows and discusses robustness and governance. Its stage-based organization is useful for comparing coverage, but does not make unlike evaluation settings directly comparable.

works.name: From AI for Science to Agentic Science: A Survey on Autonomous Scientific Discovery
works.summary: Organizes agentic science across life sciences, chemistry, materials, and physics, connecting capability, workflow, and domain perspectives. It provides a useful map of hypothesis generation, experimentation, analysis, and refinement. As a survey, its taxonomy helps navigate reported systems rather than independently reproducing their discovery or autonomy claims.

works.name: The Virtual Lab of AI agents designs new SARS-CoV-2 nanobodies
works.summary: Organizes a principal-investigator agent and scientific specialists into meetings with high-level human guidance. The agents develop a computational nanobody-design workflow, with selected designs tested experimentally. This demonstrates a specific human-AI research collaboration; human laboratory work and biological validation are central parts of the evidence.

works.name: The Ideation-Execution Gap: Execution Outcomes of LLM-Generated versus Human Research Ideas
works.summary: Recruits researchers to execute randomly assigned human- or model-generated ideas and obtains blinded reviews of the resulting projects. The apparent advantage of AI ideas at the ideation stage declines after implementation. This follow-up study shows why proposal ratings are insufficient proxies for completed research quality in its NLP setting.

works.name: AlphaEvolve: A coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery
works.summary: Evolves candidate programs using language-model edits and feedback from executable evaluators. Applications include mathematical constructions, algorithm discovery, and infrastructure optimization. The white paper illustrates breadth when a reliable scoring procedure exists; reported improvements are tied to those tasks and do not imply autonomous formulation of every scientific objective.

works.name: Biomni: A General-Purpose Biomedical AI Agent
works.summary: Combines retrieval-guided planning and executable code with an environment of biomedical tools, software, and databases. Evaluations span heterogeneous tasks, multimodal data analysis, and experimental protocol design. The reported breadth supports biomedical research assistance; benchmark performance and protocol case studies should not be treated as general clinical validation.

works.name: ScienceBoard
works.summary: Places agents in scientific software environments and evaluates 169 tasks across six domains through graphical, command-line, or mixed interactions. Programmatic checks assess outcomes in applications used for activities such as molecular analysis and geospatial work. It tests practical computer-use workflows; completing these tasks is narrower than independently conducting a sustained research program.

works.name: MOOSE-Chem2: Exploring LLM Limits in Fine-Grained Scientific Hypothesis Discovery via Hierarchical Search
works.summary: Expands coarse research directions into increasingly detailed hypotheses through hierarchical search, comparing different language-model scoring ensembles. Evaluation uses expert-annotated fine-grained hypotheses from recent literature. The study tests alignment with known hypotheses and model-defined rewards; a detailed, high-scoring proposal still needs independent checks and experimental testing.

works.name: AI-Researcher: Autonomous Scientific Innovation
works.summary: Orchestrates literature review, hypothesis formation, algorithm implementation, experiments, and manuscript preparation. It also introduces Scientist-Bench, with guided innovation and open-ended tasks derived from existing AI research. Its implementation and paper-quality evaluations help compare research pipelines; claims about innovation remain conditioned on the benchmark and evaluation protocol.

works.name: AI Idea Bench 2025
works.summary: Evaluates AI research idea generation using 3,495 target papers and their motivating references. Its protocol compares generated ideas with paper content and reference-based judgments, including novelty and feasibility assessments. Historical alignment provides a repeatable proxy for ideation quality, but resemblance to published work cannot establish prospective novelty, successful execution, or future scientific impact.

works.name: MLRC-Bench
works.summary: Evaluates proposing and implementing methods for seven challenging machine-learning research competitions using objective task metrics and constrained evaluation protocols. It directly examines the gap between judge-rated innovation and measured performance. The competition setting supports claims about research-method execution and improvement over baselines, while broader scientific importance remains outside its scoring procedure.

works.name: The AI Scientist-v2: Workshop-Level Automated Scientific Discovery via Agentic Tree Search
works.summary: Replaces fixed experiment templates with progressive agentic tree search managed by an experiment agent, and uses visual feedback to refine figures. Three generated manuscripts were submitted to an ICLR workshop, with one meeting its acceptance threshold. This provides a bounded peer-review case study rather than broad evidence of researcher replacement.

works.name: PaperBench
works.summary: Asks agents to implement and execute replications of 20 ICML 2024 papers from scratch. Author-developed hierarchical rubrics divide the work into 8,316 gradable items, with a separately assessed model-based grader. Scores indicate progress toward specified replication requirements; code-only variants, partial rubric credit, and successful empirical replication must be distinguished.

works.name: SciReplicate-Bench
works.summary: Assesses algorithm comprehension and implementation through 100 tasks extracted from 36 NLP papers published in 2024. Evaluation combines executable tests, reasoning-graph comparison, and repository dependency or API measures. Its scope is reproducing selected algorithmic components from papers; passing those tasks does not imply that every experiment or headline paper result was replicated.

works.name: AgentRxiv: Towards Collaborative Autonomous Research
works.summary: Lets agent laboratories publish and retrieve reports through a shared preprint server, allowing later research runs to build on earlier findings. Experiments on reasoning and prompting methods compare shared research against isolated agents. The measured gains concern benchmark-solving strategies, not a demonstrated open scientific community across disciplines.

works.name: BixBench
works.summary: Evaluates bioinformatics agents on more than 50 practical analysis scenarios with nearly 300 associated questions. Tasks require exploring biological datasets, performing multistep analyses, and interpreting results. Open-answer and multiple-choice settings test different behaviors; correctness on these prepared analyses should not be presented as validation of new biological mechanisms or experimental discoveries.

works.name: Agent Laboratory: Using LLM Agents as Research Assistants
works.summary: Takes a human research idea through literature review, experimentation, and report writing, producing code and a manuscript while allowing feedback at each stage. Comparisons across models and a researcher study report benefits from human guidance. The results support supervised research assistance within the tested machine-learning workflows.

works.name: AIDE
works.summary: Searches over executable machine-learning solutions by repeatedly drafting, debugging, evaluating, and improving code against a specified metric. The public reference implementation includes configuration and search-tree inspection utilities. It is a reusable experiment-search component and benchmark baseline, with results bounded by evaluator quality, data access, and safeguards against exploiting the evaluation setup.

works.name: OpenEvolve
works.summary: An open community implementation inspired by AlphaEvolve that evolves programs using language models, evaluator feedback, and population-based search. It includes examples for mathematical optimization, scientific computing, and kernel improvement. The repository is independently maintained rather than Google's original system, and its reported improvements should be checked against the corresponding evaluator and hardware conditions.

works.name: R&D-Agent
works.summary: Separates research proposal generation from development and evaluation, then iterates using experimental feedback. Microsoft's public project includes data-science, model-development, and quantitative-finance scenarios. It offers a practical architecture for automating repeated implementation work; success in an included scenario does not establish broad scientific discovery ability or transfer to unrelated domains.

works.name: ShinkaEvolve
works.summary: Combines language-model program mutations with evolutionary search, solution archives, and evaluation feedback to improve algorithms. The public framework supports local or cluster evaluation and tasks with executable verifiers. It is suited to measurable algorithm discovery, with scientific conclusions limited by what the verifier and optimization objective actually test.

works.name: ToolUniverse
works.summary: Provides a common interface for scientific tools, datasets, models, and APIs so language-model agents can discover and invoke external capabilities. The public project offers a Python SDK and agent integrations. It supplies infrastructure for building scientific assistants; available tool connectors do not by themselves establish reliable tool selection, valid analyses, or experimental reproducibility.

works.name: Autonomous LLM-driven research from data to human-verifiable research papers
works.summary: Guides agents from annotated data through hypotheses, analysis code, results, and a manuscript while tracing information backward to its sources. The study reports stronger reliability for simpler goals and limited novelty, with human co-piloting increasingly important as complexity rises. Traceability is a central design feature rather than an afterthought.

works.name: RE-Bench
works.summary: Compares agents with human experts on seven open-ended machine-learning research engineering environments, including optimization tasks with executable scoring functions. Its human-attempt data and multiple time budgets make resource assumptions visible. Results concern bounded AI research engineering, and rankings can change with time allowance; they do not establish general scientific autonomy.

works.name: CycleResearcher: Improving Automated Research via Automated Review
works.summary: Trains research-writing and reviewing models in a feedback cycle using research and peer-review datasets. Generated papers are refined through simulated review, with evaluations of score prediction and manuscript ratings. Those simulated ratings measure an important writing-and-review capability, but should not be interpreted as independently executed experiments or scientific discoveries.

works.name: MLE-bench
works.summary: Packages 75 Kaggle competitions to assess dataset preparation, model training, and iterative experimentation, with historical leaderboard thresholds as reference points. Useful for engineering-focused research agents and resource-scaling studies. A competition medal measures predictive performance under a particular setup; it is not evidence of novel hypotheses or scientific validity beyond that task.

works.name: MOOSE-Chem: Large Language Models for Rediscovering Unseen Chemistry Scientific Hypotheses
works.summary: Decomposes hypothesis discovery into retrieving inspirations, composing hypotheses, and ranking them. A chemist-annotated benchmark uses papers published after the evaluated model's stated training cutoff to test rediscovery. Similarity to withheld published hypotheses measures a useful capability, but does not establish prospective novelty or successful laboratory realization.

works.name: ScienceAgentBench
works.summary: Contains 102 expert-validated tasks derived from 44 publications across four disciplines. Each task requires a self-contained Python program, assessed through code, execution outputs, and costs. The benchmark deliberately tests individual data-driven research steps, providing a stronger basis for bounded capability claims than treating generated manuscripts as evidence of complete scientific discovery.

works.name: Scideator: Human-LLM Compound System for Scientific Ideation through Facet Recombination and Novelty Evaluation
works.summary: Extracts purpose, mechanism, and evaluation facets from papers, lets researchers recombine them, and retrieves related work to assess originality. The updated paper reports creativity-support benefits and novelty-checking ablations. Its contribution is an interactive ideation process, with user judgments and retrieval quality distinct from validating a finished scientific result.

works.name: CORE-Bench
works.summary: Measures computational reproducibility using supplied code and data: 270 tasks from 90 papers across computer science, social science, and medicine, with three difficulty levels. Agents must recover results and answer questions about them. Re-running artifacts does not validate the underlying scientific claims; the 2026 follow-up introduces v1.1 and out-of-distribution tasks after auditing shortcuts.

works.name: PaperQA2
works.summary: An agentic retrieval system for answering scientific questions with cited evidence from documents. It combines paper search, metadata collection, contextual evidence summaries, and iterative answer generation, with a public Python package and command-line interface. The research reports strong literature-task performance; those results concern particular evaluations rather than guaranteed factual correctness for every answer.

works.name: SciAgents: Automating scientific discovery through multi-agent intelligent graph reasoning
works.summary: Combines ontological knowledge graphs, retrieval tools, and collaborating language-model agents to propose and critique interdisciplinary hypotheses. Biologically inspired materials case studies illustrate connections between concepts and proposed mechanisms. The primary evidence is hypothesis-generation and reasoning case studies, which should be separated from laboratory verification of resulting material designs.

works.name: Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with 100+ NLP Researchers
works.summary: Uses blinded comparisons between researcher-written and agent-generated NLP ideas, involving more than one hundred researchers. AI ideas receive higher novelty judgments but weaker feasibility judgments, while self-evaluation and diversity remain problematic. The experiment evaluates perceived idea quality, not whether executing those ideas yields stronger scientific discoveries.

works.name: The AI Scientist: Towards Fully Automated Open-Ended Scientific Discovery
works.summary: Connects idea generation, code editing, experiments, visualization, manuscript drafting, and automated reviewing around human-provided research templates. Demonstrations cover diffusion models, language models, and learning dynamics. Paper-quality claims rely substantially on an automated reviewer, and the template dependence bounds the extent of open-ended autonomy demonstrated.

works.name: SciCode
works.summary: Uses 80 scientist-authored research coding problems, decomposed into 338 subproblems across 16 subfields, to test scientific knowledge and executable implementation. Report main-problem and subproblem accuracy separately, including whether background information was supplied. This assesses specified computational tasks; the later SciCode-Verified audit also makes benchmark version and test defects relevant to comparisons.

works.name: LAB-Bench
works.summary: Provides more than 2,400 multiple-choice questions targeting practical biology-research capabilities, including literature reasoning, figure interpretation, database navigation, and sequence manipulation. Expert comparisons help contextualize performance on research-adjacent tasks. These are bounded question-answer evaluations, so high scores alone do not demonstrate reliable laboratory execution, end-to-end biological research, or novel experimental validation.

works.name: DiscoveryBench
works.summary: Tests hypothesis discovery from supplied datasets, metadata, and natural-language goals using 264 literature-derived tasks across six domains, plus 903 synthetic tasks. Facet-based evaluation separates aspects of a proposed finding. The target is recovering supported relationships within provided data, with synthetic and real tasks reported separately, rather than discovering unrestricted new scientific knowledge.

works.name: BioDiscoveryAgent: An AI Agent for Designing Genetic Perturbation Experiments
works.summary: Selects genetic perturbations using language-model knowledge, literature search, code analysis, and critique, then updates proposals from experimental outcomes. Evaluation across perturbation datasets compares it with Bayesian optimization and random selection. The evidence concerns efficient experiment selection in the tested settings rather than autonomous validation of arbitrary biological mechanisms.

works.name: ChemCrow: Augmenting large language models with chemistry tools
works.summary: Augments a language model with expert-designed chemistry tools for synthesis, molecular tasks, and materials design. The work includes executed synthesis examples and expert assessment. Its preprint also highlights weaknesses in using a language model to judge chemical correctness, underscoring why tool execution and independent expert evaluation matter.

works.name: ResearchAgent: Iterative Research Idea Generation over Scientific Literature with Large Language Models
works.summary: Expands a seed paper through an academic graph and a concept store, then iteratively refines proposed problems, methods, and experimental designs using reviewing agents. Human and model evaluations cover multiple disciplines. The demonstrated output is a research proposal; executing the experiments and validating its scientific claims remain separate tasks.

works.name: Docling
works.summary: Converts PDFs and other documents into structured representations for retrieval and downstream analysis, including layout-aware extraction and handling of tables and figures. Its open implementation supports research-document ingestion. It is an enabling component rather than a scientist agent; extraction quality should be checked before treating parsed tables, formulas, or reading order as reliable evidence.

works.name: MLAgentBench
works.summary: Evaluates agents that read and modify files, run experiments, and inspect results across 13 machine-learning tasks, from CIFAR-10 improvement to BabyLM. Task success exposes planning and experimentation failures within supplied problems; it does not measure autonomous selection of important research questions or independently validated scientific discoveries.

works.name: OpenScholar
works.summary: Pairs scientific retrieval with a language model trained to synthesize evidence and attach supporting citations. The authors provide implementation resources, models, data, and scientific question-answering evaluations, with a later Nature publication. It is a foundation for literature-grounded assistants; retrieval coverage and citation quality remain properties to evaluate for each downstream corpus and task.

works.name: STORM / Co-STORM
works.summary: Builds sourced topic outlines and long-form articles by combining retrieval with questions from multiple perspectives. Co-STORM adds collaborative discussion and a shared concept map so users can steer exploration. The official implementation is useful for research preparation and knowledge curation; its authors explicitly note that generated articles often require substantial editing.

works.name: Coscientist: Autonomous chemical research with large language models
works.summary: Connects language-model planning to web and documentation search, code execution, and experimental equipment. Demonstrations include chemical synthesis planning and reaction optimization, illustrating how tool access can turn reasoning into physical experiments. The work operates within a configured laboratory and selected tasks, with human setup and oversight remaining important.

works.name: FunSearch: Mathematical discoveries from program search with large language models
works.summary: Pairs a language model with an evaluator and an evolving database of programs, searching for code that constructs strong solutions. The paper reports new cap-set constructions and improved bin-packing heuristics. Its successes depend on explicit evaluators and problem specifications, making the verification mechanism central to its scientific relevance.

works.name: GPT Researcher
works.summary: A configurable research agent that decomposes questions, gathers evidence from web or local sources, and assembles cited reports. It exposes a package, interfaces, and multi-agent or recursive research workflows. It is useful as a general research component, but its project-level claims should not be confused with scientific novelty or independently validated literature-review completeness.

works.name: SciMON: Scientific Inspiration Machines Optimized for Novelty
works.summary: Retrieves scientific inspirations and iteratively revises proposed ideas by comparing them with prior literature. Its contextual idea-generation setting goes beyond predicting links between concepts. Human-oriented evaluations show improvements over baseline generation while also exposing limited technical depth and novelty, making it useful for studying ideation quality rather than experimental discovery.

works.name: ASReview LAB
works.summary: Uses active learning to prioritize records during systematic literature screening while preserving human inclusion decisions. It provides a screening interface, simulation tools, label management, and exportable review state. This is a complementary evidence-selection tool rather than a generative scientist; screening completeness depends on the review protocol, labels, and stopping decision.

works.name: The Automation of Science (Robot Scientist Adam)
works.summary: Combines hypothesis generation, automated laboratory experiments, and a logical record of the research process to study yeast functional genomics. The authors report manual confirmation of Adam's conclusions. This pre-LLM example grounds modern autonomy discussions in a closed experimental loop and explicit provenance within a constrained biological problem.

records.name: RIDAR
records.summary: Provides trajectory collectors, post-hoc integrity detection, runtime intervention, and a monitoring interface for research agents. Findings link to evidence in recorded runs, with public result files accompanying the implementation. It supports investigation of agent research behavior; detector output requires contextual review and does not certify scientific validity.
records.status: Official repository announces the code release on 23 October. No installation or runtime validation was performed here.

records.name: ADAPT for Science: A Multi-Agent System for Self-Evolving Scientific Optimization
records.summary: Combines retrieval of historical scientific designs, evolving start-selection strategies, and optimizer-program evolution under physical constraints. The authors evaluate gravitational-wave detector designs on eight held-out topologies using a differentiable simulator and matched scientific evaluation budgets. Results support optimization within this setting; transfer beyond simulation and dependence on historical-library coverage remain open.

records.name: GeoAgent: Contract-Constrained LLM Agents for Seismic Data Processing
records.summary: Connects seismic-processing tools through a fixed nine-stage graph, with explicit contracts for artifacts, input resolution, parameter ownership, and output validation. Deterministic geometry checks address failures that prompting alone did not prevent. Evidence comes from engineering measurements on one dataset and model family; adaptive planning, migration quality, and broader controlled comparisons remain unestablished.

records.name: RIDAR: Safeguarding Research Integrity in Autonomous Research Agents via Automated Detection and Runtime Intervention
records.summary: Audits research trajectories with separate Analyzer and Verifier agents, then tests runtime feedback against matched unassisted runs. Its taxonomy covers 14 integrity violations. Reported findings depend on LLM judgments and mathematics/ML tasks; testing files and extra resources remain accessible deliberately, so detected violation rates should not be generalized to environments enforcing those boundaries.
records.status: Annotation follows the October arXiv preprint. An earlier ICLR 2027 submission was withdrawn; its title and reported results differ.

records.name: RIV-Gold
records.summary: Contains 60 research-agent trajectories annotated by 17 experts using the RIVT integrity taxonomy. Evaluation distinguishes finding-level matching from exact violation-type agreement, making it useful for testing trajectory auditors. The sampled mathematics and ML tasks constrain generalization; agreement with annotations is distinct from proving that a resulting scientific claim is correct.
records.status: Public auditor code and result files were verified; release of the full raw trajectories and annotation package was not established.

records.name: Astro2Method
records.summary: Tests machine-learning method selection with 500 expert-reviewed binary questions derived from 346 astronomy papers. Questions distinguish complete from partial methodological explanations. Historical retrieval and additional agent reasoning do not consistently improve accuracy; web-search gains concentrate on finding the source papers. This measures retrospective method judgments, not executing alternative methods or establishing prospective astronomical discoveries.
records.status: The official dataset card exposes 500 test rows under CC BY 4.0. No dataset files were downloaded and no evaluation was run.

records.name: ExpEvolve: Structuring and Reusing Experience for Open-Ended Discovery
records.summary: Extracts interpretable idea factors from archived programs whose score differences remain unexplained, then uses bandit-selected edits and plateau-triggered exploration to guide program evolution. Evaluations cover eleven mathematical tasks and six machine-learning engineering tasks. Reported gains concern bounded executable objectives; the theoretical benefits require stated assumptions, and transfer to expensive scientific verification remains untested.
records.status: The paper identifies itself as an extended version of CausalEvolve (arXiv:2603.14575). An official implementation release was not established from the inspected sources.

records.name: GAV: A scientific experimentation environment for PDE agents
records.summary: Learns continuous reference solutions and constructs matching PDE problems through manufactured solutions, giving coding agents numerical feedback without solving every new reference problem. Evaluations cover Navier–Stokes and Vlasov–Poisson-type tasks and adaptations of existing PDE agents. Its reliability analysis assumes controlled distribution mismatch and independent evaluation data; success on generated problems does not establish accuracy across arbitrary physical regimes.

records.name: Recursive Flint
records.summary: An open-weight mixture-of-experts coding model built with Recursive’s Eureka Machine and a human team. The model card specifies 39.8B total parameters and approximately 2.5B active per token, including the output head. Included as a concrete automated-research output and reusable coding component; released weights and inference code do not independently validate the development process or reported performance.
records.status: Apache-2.0 weights and inference engine; no local execution or independent performance reproduction in this collection.

records.name: Agent4Sci
records.summary: Combines 25 tasks from 20 scientific ML benchmarks across 11 domains. Human-verified baselines and standardized environments support agent optimization, separate held-out evaluation, and trajectory auditing. It probes scientific hill-climbing under declared compute budgets; variable long-horizon runs and imperfect verification limit leaderboard interpretations and broader claims of autonomous discovery.
records.status: Public runner and author-linked data splits; underlying datasets retain their individual terms. No execution was performed here.

records.name: Automating ML for Science: Can Frontier Agents Climb Scientific Hills in the Wild?
records.summary: Studies frontier coding agents improving scientific ML baselines in Agent4Sci, separating optimization, held-out evaluation, and trajectory auditing. Default gains are largely engineering-driven; targeted research skills produce more varied interventions. The study distinguishes metric improvement from scientific insight, with limitations from run variance, imperfect audits, task-specific skills, and the absence of a human-researcher baseline.
records.status: The arXiv comment names the NeurIPS 2026 E&D Track; a proceedings record was not verified, so the source label remains preprint.

records.name: Autonomous adaptive spectral analysis with an LLM agent for self-driving laboratories
records.summary: Uses an LLM to inspect spectra and diagnostics, adjust predefined fitting parameters within bounded retries, or abstain, while deterministic code calculates the physical quantity. On 203 archived film spectra, it retains 183 baseline values, recovers 16 failed analyses, and abstains on four. This retrospective, single-campaign study does not test live laboratory control or detection of physically incorrect results that pass numerical checks.
records.status: Linked code belongs to the earlier deterministic optical-analysis campaign. Agent instructions are in this paper’s supplementary information; a standalone release of the complete agent workflow was not established.

records.name: Bayesian Model Discovery with Language Models: Closing the Loop between Hypotheses and Experiments
records.summary: Combines LLM-proposed functional forms with numerical parameter fitting, evidence-weighted predictions, and experiment selection by joint information gain over models and parameters. Four benchmarks compare predictive error and structural recovery, with ablations of numerical feedback. Results depend on the candidate pool, priors, and observation model; containing the true law as a special case is explicitly distinguished from recovering its exact form.
records.status: Preprint v1 inspected. No official implementation release was established from the examined primary sources.

records.name: Magnolia: A Persistent-Memory Agent Framework for Computational Chemistry
records.summary: Combines computational chemistry tools with session records, confirmed project knowledge, and human-reviewed rules reused across projects. Four case studies and controlled replays of four internal tasks examine the contribution of retained context. The authors explicitly position it as supervised research assistance; campaign-wide memory benefits remain unisolated, and complete docking records include unreleased collaborator results.

records.name: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
records.summary: Extracts atomic claims from published cancer-registry studies, executes reproduction analyses, and tests alternative analytical choices through agent-generated perturbations. SEER-Repro supplies the evaluation setting. The authors distinguish reproducing reported findings from assessing their sensitivity; flagged alternatives require expert review, and report-based grading does not independently verify the complete analysis code.

records.name: DFM-Bench
records.summary: Evaluates hypotheses, revisions, development paths, complete research runs, and contribution families, with computational delivery tracked separately. The public runner imports snapshots and prepares evidence packets for external judging. Proposal scores and contribution records do not confirm discoveries; the paper reports correlated AI review roles and pending independent calibration of the automated evaluator.

records.name: DiscoveryRSI
records.summary: Provides a public research harness with provider adapters, role prompts, a tool registry, replay storage, and domain adapters for hypothesis development. The accompanying DiscoveryRSI-27B checkpoint supports research planning and revision. Public components expose the workflow, but restricted datasets and private campaign traces are excluded; this collection has not executed the system.

records.name: DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses
records.summary: Develops hypothesis trees through multi-agent search, compiles selected investigations into Harbor tasks, and improves subsequent research through contribution-weighted model training and workflow replay. DFM-Bench assesses proposals and their development. Reported gains concern hypothesis quality and retrospective literature correspondence; these measures do not establish independently validated discoveries or causal influence on later publications.
records.status: Summary follows v2, revised 20 October 2026; date records the first submission on 16 October.

records.name: SEER-Repro
records.summary: Evaluates reproduction of 2,190 atomic claims from 20 published SEER-based studies using database documentation and executable analyses. Numerical tolerances and model-assisted evidence grading determine claim outcomes. Scores concern the selected papers and available registry release; matching reported claims does not establish robustness to alternative analyses or independent verification of all code.
records.status: Benchmark described in the preprint; a public code and benchmark-package release was not verified in the inspected sources.

records.name: PhysClosureBench
records.summary: Provides 50 physics research tasks with specified goals and constraints. A 20-criterion score measures local accomplishments, while a separate closure assessment tests whether essential evidence and applicability conditions resolve the research question. Model-based grading includes a selected human consistency check; high partial scores are not equivalent to complete scientific closure.
records.status: Execution framework and Case 30 example are public; the author-linked Hugging Face page provides the 50-case materials. Scientific grading is separate from the execution harness.

records.name: SciPIvot
records.summary: Tests scientific judgment through 248 decisions drawn from human corrections across 26 research projects. Models choose between an original agent plan and a human-corrected alternative, with or without the prior project record. This evaluates recognition of selected corrective decisions, not plan generation, research execution, or the prevalence of failures across scientific work.

records.name: Agentic Scientist
records.summary: Orchestrates coding agents through investigation, ablations, sealed evaluation, analysis, and manuscript production. The public implementation includes task snapshots, resumable runs, and an inspection interface. It is useful for studying research orchestration and evidence collection; successful execution and scientific validity still depend on the task, evaluator, and underlying agent.

records.name: The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery
records.summary: Coordinates coding agents through task drafting, ideas, sandboxed experiments, baselines, ablations, analysis, and manuscript writing. A meta-controller enforces stage-specific rubrics. The paper reports computational discovery studies and an ALIFE 2026 paper produced in a co-scientist setting; that human collaboration should be distinguished from its separate autonomous evaluations.

records.name: Can AI Scientists Coordinate at Runtime?
records.summary: Adds runtime agent selection, scoped work contracts, and artifact-based verification to existing scientist frameworks. A single-seed exploratory study compares cumulative coordination variants under host-calibrated budgets. Runtime selection gives the strongest observed means, while additional contracts and verification can reduce scores, exposing tradeoffs that larger replicated evaluations should investigate.

records.name: Denario Project: Deep Knowledge Artificial Intelligence Agents for Scientific Discovery
records.summary: Provides modular agents for ideation, literature checking, planning, code execution, plotting, writing, and reviewing, using Cmbagent for analysis. Demonstrations span multiple scientific disciplines and include domain-expert reviews of generated drafts. The authors position it as a research assistant, with case-study quality and limitations requiring inspection of each output.

records.name: Agentic AI–Physicist Collaboration in Experimental Particle Physics: A Proof-of-Concept Measurement with LEP Open Data
records.summary: Demonstrates an agent-assisted thrust measurement from archived ALEPH collision data, including code execution, unfolding, uncertainty propagation, and manuscript drafting. Physicists supply prior analyses and context, define acceptance criteria, inspect results, and approve major decisions. The published contribution is a supervised analysis demonstration using a known observable, not an autonomous discovery or a controlled estimate of productivity gains.
records.status: Published in Highlights of High-Energy Physics, volume 2, issue 3, article 10, on 30 September 2026. The first preprint appeared on 5 March; v3 incorporates journal proofreading corrections.

records.name: ScientistTwo
records.summary: Coordinates idea generation, experimental evaluation, ablation analysis, manuscript writing, and internal review in a closed research loop. The project releases generated research artifacts and reports benchmark comparisons, integrity audits, automated reviews, and human manuscript evaluation. These are author-reported results; the public project page does not establish availability of the complete framework source.

records.name: ScientistTwo: Pioneering the Human Knowledge Frontier with Autonomous AI
records.summary: Starts from a research problem, establishes baselines, proposes hypotheses, runs experiments and ablations, and iterates through simulated reviews. Evaluation includes publication-derived machine-learning tasks, integrity audits, automated reviewers, and a human study of generated papers. These complementary author-reported assessments remain bounded by the selected tasks; simulated acceptance is distinct from actual venue acceptance.

records.name: ScienceBuddy
records.summary: Combines an interactive scientific workspace with research on alternating harness improvement and model reinforcement learning. The public repository distinguishes its hosted workspace demonstration from open experiments using frozen tasks and simulated feedback. It is especially relevant to human feedback and persistent research context; deployed continual improvement is not established by the released experiment alone.

records.name: ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents
records.summary: Turns researcher requests, feedback, and execution traces into learning tasks and evaluation rubrics. An inner loop adapts the agent harness while an outer loop trains the model under the improved harness. Case studies cover four scientific task families; they demonstrate the proposed learning workflow rather than universal autonomous discovery.

records.name: IdeaForecastBench
records.summary: Evaluates whether ideas proposed from literature available before a cutoff correspond to later publications. It contains 624 rolling episodes across 52 topics, generates up to five ranked ideas, and reports separate judge results. This measures research forecasting under a retrospective protocol; broad or generic predictions and judge sensitivity complicate interpretation as precise scientific anticipation.
records.status: The arXiv record reports acceptance to EMNLP 2026; a proceedings record was not located during this check.

records.name: ResearchStudio
records.summary: Microsoft's research skill collection includes Idea for developing literature-grounded research proposals and Reel for turning completed papers into posters, narrated videos, blogs, and interactive presentations. The code exposes editable workflows for coding agents. Its two modules support different stages of research and communication; their presence does not establish an autonomous experimental discovery pipeline.

records.name: Recursive Eureka Machine
records.summary: Recursive describes an automated research loop that proposes ideas, implements experiments, checks results, and carries useful context across parallel investigations. Public examples include training and GPU-kernel optimization; its later Flint model provides a released development outcome. Available research artifacts support inspection of selected outputs, but do not establish access to the complete research framework or independently verified autonomy.
records.status: Creator-reported system; public output artifacts are distinct from full framework source.

records.name: SoundnessBench
records.summary: Tests methodological judgments on 1,099 results-masked research proposals reconstructed from ICLR papers. Reviewer soundness scores provide proxy labels; 327 proposals also have proposal-only expert judgments. It separates false approvals from false rejections. Full-paper reviewers and proposal-only assessors see different evidence, and subjective labels limit interpretation as ground truth for scientific soundness.
records.status: Public proposal dataset and evaluation code verified. The v2 expert subset is described in the paper; its separate annotation release was not verified.

records.name: SoundnessBench: Can Your AI Scientist Really Tell Good Research Ideas from Bad Ones?
records.summary: Examines whether language models can assess methodological soundness before experiments are run. Results-masked proposals receive reviewer-derived proxy labels and separate expert judgments on a subset. Standard prompts favor approval, while aggressive prompts trade false approvals for false rejections. The study concerns proposal-stage judgment; its labels do not establish experimental truth or general research quality.
records.status: Reviewed v2, revised 22 October 2026; date retains the first arXiv submission on 28 May.

records.name: ScientistOne
records.summary: Connects literature investigation, algorithm discovery, writing, and claim verification through explicit evidence chains. Its accompanying audit checks scores, specification compliance, references, and agreement between methods and code. Generated papers and solver code are public; availability of the complete research framework was not confirmed. Reported integrity results are from the authors' evaluation.

records.name: ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence
records.summary: Maintains explicit evidence chains from literature and experiments to manuscript claims, with audits for score reproduction, specification violations, references, and method-code agreement. The authors compare generated papers across research tasks and report improved integrity. These are task-specific audits, so the title's human-level claim should not be generalized to all research.

records.name: Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist
records.summary: Uses specialized agents to generate, criticize, rank, and evolve hypotheses through tournaments, with scientists setting goals and steering exploration. The Nature paper includes biomedical applications and laboratory validation of selected hypotheses. The system supports scientific reasoning; experimental validation remains a distinct process rather than an automatically closed physical loop.

records.name: Empirical Research Assistance: An AI system to help scientists write expert-level empirical software
records.summary: Uses language-model code mutations and tree search to improve a specified empirical quality metric, incorporating research ideas from external sources. The Nature paper evaluates diverse scientific software tasks, including bioinformatics and forecasting. Its strength is experimentally scored implementation search; results depend on the supplied objectives, evaluation data, and task design.

records.name: Robin: A multi-agent system for automating scientific discovery
records.summary: Combines literature agents and data-analysis agents in an iterative hypothesis, experiment, and interpretation cycle. The Nature study reports in-vitro evidence for candidate interventions affecting retinal-cell phagocytosis. Human researchers perform the physical experiments, and these preclinical findings do not establish treatment effectiveness in patients.

records.name: PaperOrchestra
records.summary: Transforms research ideas, experimental records, and formatting requirements into LaTeX manuscripts through specialized planning, literature, plotting, writing, and refinement agents. The official Google Research repository accompanies the paper and evaluation resources. It addresses synthesis of existing research materials; manuscript quality ratings do not verify that the underlying experiments or scientific conclusions are correct.

records.name: Towards end-to-end automation of AI research
records.summary: Integrates the AI Scientist lineage into a journal study of template-based and template-free research workflows, including idea generation, experiments, writing, and reviewing. A generated manuscript passed an initial workshop review round. This peer-reviewed system paper should be distinguished from the separate question of whether generated findings are independently replicated.

records.name: RINoBench
records.summary: Tests research-idea novelty judgments with 1,381 expert-derived ideas and nine metrics covering numerical novelty ratings and written justifications. The authors find that human-like explanations can coexist with inaccurate novelty judgments. This is useful for evaluating critic or reviewer agents, while novelty-rating agreement remains distinct from feasibility, empirical correctness, and discovery value.

records.name: EvoScientist: Towards Multi-Agent Evolving AI Scientists for End-to-End Scientific Discovery
records.summary: Separates research, engineering, and evolution-management roles, storing both ideation history and experiment lessons in persistent memory. The October 2026 revision reports gains in idea assessment and code-execution success. These evaluations support reuse of research experience, while broader discovery quality still requires inspection beyond successful code execution.

records.name: MOOSE-Star: Unlocking Tractable Training for Scientific Discovery by Breaking the Complexity Barrier
records.summary: Trains hypothesis generation through decomposed discovery subtasks, motivation-guided hierarchical retrieval, and bounded composition. It releases TOMATO-Star and studies scaling with training data and inference budget. The claimed complexity reduction depends on the paper's assumptions and best-case analysis; benchmark scaling is distinct from prospective experimental validation.

records.name: AutoIllustrate
records.summary: Converts a method description into an editable draw.io diagram, then optionally applies an image-generation restyling pass. The public command-line workflow includes figure generation and visual auditing and was used with Agentic Scientist. Retaining the vector source supports manual correction, but generated visual polish should not be taken as evidence of methodological fidelity.

records.name: Autonomous Research Agents: A Survey of AI Scientists and the Verification Gap
records.summary: Examines computational research agents through autonomy, evaluation, released artifacts, human intervention, novelty checks, and result-selection disclosure. Its coded corpus distinguishes runnable code from evidence that supports scientific claims. The conclusions are bounded by the screened AI/ML systems and coding rules, rather than a census of all scientific domains.

records.name: Magnolia
records.summary: Adds readable project notebooks, reviewed memory promotion, scientific-tool wrappers, and local or Slurm job tracking to an OpenCode-based workflow. Two MCP services expose memory and computational operations while preserving run provenance. Researchers direct the work and approve standing rules; the claim critic and promotion panel do not establish scientific correctness, and adaptation to another harness requires additional integration.
records.status: Public research software; no installation or execution was performed. The paper explicitly disclaims autonomy, so the catalog treats this as supporting research infrastructure. Precise initial release date not established.

records.name: OpenResearch
records.summary: A local research workspace and harness from alphaXiv that connects coding agents to literature discovery, experiment execution, and artifact inspection. It records experiments in a local database and supports multiple compute backends. The repository documents a usable product; these capabilities are project claims rather than an independently established discovery benchmark.

records.name: PaperBanana
records.summary: Uses retrieval, planning, styling, visualization, and critique agents to generate academic diagrams and plots from scientific content. Its repository includes execution interfaces and a benchmark of reference illustrations. It is a useful study of iterative visual communication, with semantic accuracy and faithful representation of experimental data still requiring inspection beyond aesthetic judgments.

records.name: PDE-GAV
records.summary: Provides a configurable PDE experimentation environment with public-input queries, private reference evaluation, candidate selection, run logs, and interfaces for new equations and tasks. The repository documents a deterministic CPU demonstration and scientific campaign configurations. Large datasets, weights, and complete historical execution archives are external; public code availability alone does not reproduce the paper’s experiments.
records.status: Official repository and documentation inspected without installation or execution. Only the release year is recorded; a precise initial software-release date was not established.

records.name: AInsteinBench
records.summary: Evaluates scientific software development using tasks derived from maintainer pull requests across six research codebases. Executable tests assess changes in domains including chemistry, molecular dynamics, and numerical relativity. This measures repository-level implementation and verification under specified tests; it does not assess autonomous hypothesis selection or establish correctness beyond the tested behavior.
records.status: Public evaluation code and question files; the README states that Docker images for Multi-SWE-bench-format questions are available upon request.

records.name: FrontierScience
records.summary: Assesses expert-level physics, chemistry, and biology reasoning using Olympiad and Research splits. The released gold sets contain 100 short-answer questions and 60 research subtasks, with model grading against answers or rubrics. These constrained, expert-authored tasks probe scientific reasoning; the creators explicitly distinguish them from the broader work of producing new discoveries.

records.name: Kosmos
records.summary: Combines literature-search and data-analysis agents with a structured world model that preserves information across long investigations. Edison provides the system through a hosted platform and reports discovery case studies with traceable supporting evidence. Reported productivity equivalents come from user estimates and modeling assumptions, rather than a controlled general measure of researcher replacement.

records.name: Kosmos: An AI Scientist for Autonomous Discovery
records.summary: Uses a structured world model to coordinate repeated literature search and data-analysis trajectories from an objective and dataset. Reports link claims to code or literature, and the paper presents seven discovery case studies with external scientist assessments. Human-equivalent time estimates are collaborator judgments rather than controlled productivity measurements.

records.name: A Survey of AI Scientists
records.summary: Synthesizes AI-scientist systems through six stages covering literature, ideas, preparation, execution, writing, and paper generation. The revised survey traces the shift from individual components to integrated workflows and discusses robustness and governance. Its stage-based organization is useful for comparing coverage, but does not make unlike evaluation settings directly comparable.

records.name: From AI for Science to Agentic Science: A Survey on Autonomous Scientific Discovery
records.summary: Organizes agentic science across life sciences, chemistry, materials, and physics, connecting capability, workflow, and domain perspectives. It provides a useful map of hypothesis generation, experimentation, analysis, and refinement. As a survey, its taxonomy helps navigate reported systems rather than independently reproducing their discovery or autonomy claims.

records.name: The Virtual Lab of AI agents designs new SARS-CoV-2 nanobodies
records.summary: Organizes a principal-investigator agent and scientific specialists into meetings with high-level human guidance. The agents develop a computational nanobody-design workflow, with selected designs tested experimentally. This demonstrates a specific human-AI research collaboration; human laboratory work and biological validation are central parts of the evidence.

records.name: The Ideation-Execution Gap: Execution Outcomes of LLM-Generated versus Human Research Ideas
records.summary: Recruits researchers to execute randomly assigned human- or model-generated ideas and obtains blinded reviews of the resulting projects. The apparent advantage of AI ideas at the ideation stage declines after implementation. This follow-up study shows why proposal ratings are insufficient proxies for completed research quality in its NLP setting.

records.name: AlphaEvolve: A coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery
records.summary: Evolves candidate programs using language-model edits and feedback from executable evaluators. Applications include mathematical constructions, algorithm discovery, and infrastructure optimization. The white paper illustrates breadth when a reliable scoring procedure exists; reported improvements are tied to those tasks and do not imply autonomous formulation of every scientific objective.

records.name: Biomni: A General-Purpose Biomedical AI Agent
records.summary: Combines retrieval-guided planning and executable code with an environment of biomedical tools, software, and databases. Evaluations span heterogeneous tasks, multimodal data analysis, and experimental protocol design. The reported breadth supports biomedical research assistance; benchmark performance and protocol case studies should not be treated as general clinical validation.

records.name: ScienceBoard
records.summary: Places agents in scientific software environments and evaluates 169 tasks across six domains through graphical, command-line, or mixed interactions. Programmatic checks assess outcomes in applications used for activities such as molecular analysis and geospatial work. It tests practical computer-use workflows; completing these tasks is narrower than independently conducting a sustained research program.

records.name: MOOSE-Chem2: Exploring LLM Limits in Fine-Grained Scientific Hypothesis Discovery via Hierarchical Search
records.summary: Expands coarse research directions into increasingly detailed hypotheses through hierarchical search, comparing different language-model scoring ensembles. Evaluation uses expert-annotated fine-grained hypotheses from recent literature. The study tests alignment with known hypotheses and model-defined rewards; a detailed, high-scoring proposal still needs independent checks and experimental testing.

records.name: AI-Researcher: Autonomous Scientific Innovation
records.summary: Orchestrates literature review, hypothesis formation, algorithm implementation, experiments, and manuscript preparation. It also introduces Scientist-Bench, with guided innovation and open-ended tasks derived from existing AI research. Its implementation and paper-quality evaluations help compare research pipelines; claims about innovation remain conditioned on the benchmark and evaluation protocol.

records.name: Scientist-Bench
records.summary: Introduced with AI-Researcher, this benchmark derives guided innovation and open-ended exploration tasks from AI research papers, supplying references, instructions, and datasets. The initial paper evaluates 22 reference papers and six open-ended tasks. Implementation assessments and comparative manuscript judgments cover several workflow stages, but judge-rated similarity to human research is not independent confirmation of novel scientific findings.

records.name: AI Idea Bench 2025
records.summary: Evaluates AI research idea generation using 3,495 target papers and their motivating references. Its protocol compares generated ideas with paper content and reference-based judgments, including novelty and feasibility assessments. Historical alignment provides a repeatable proxy for ideation quality, but resemblance to published work cannot establish prospective novelty, successful execution, or future scientific impact.

records.name: MLRC-Bench
records.summary: Evaluates proposing and implementing methods for seven challenging machine-learning research competitions using objective task metrics and constrained evaluation protocols. It directly examines the gap between judge-rated innovation and measured performance. The competition setting supports claims about research-method execution and improvement over baselines, while broader scientific importance remains outside its scoring procedure.

records.name: The AI Scientist-v2
records.summary: Uses an experiment manager and progressive tree search to explore research implementations without fixed starting templates.
