It integrates experiments, figures, manuscript writing, and review. The later Nature evaluation describes human selection of workshop submissions and withdrawal after review; workshop scores therefore should not be interpreted as an entirely unselected autonomous publication pipeline.

records.name: The AI Scientist-v2: Workshop-Level Automated Scientific Discovery via Agentic Tree Search
records.summary: Replaces fixed experiment templates with progressive agentic tree search managed by an experiment agent, and uses visual feedback to refine figures. Three generated manuscripts were submitted to an ICLR workshop, with one meeting its acceptance threshold. This provides a bounded peer-review case study rather than broad evidence of researcher replacement.

records.name: PaperBench
records.summary: Asks agents to implement and execute replications of 20 ICML 2024 papers from scratch. Author-developed hierarchical rubrics divide the work into 8,316 gradable items, with a separately assessed model-based grader. Scores indicate progress toward specified replication requirements; code-only variants, partial rubric credit, and successful empirical replication must be distinguished.

records.name: SciReplicate-Bench
records.summary: Assesses algorithm comprehension and implementation through 100 tasks extracted from 36 NLP papers published in 2024. Evaluation combines executable tests, reasoning-graph comparison, and repository dependency or API measures. Its scope is reproducing selected algorithmic components from papers; passing those tasks does not imply that every experiment or headline paper result was replicated.

records.name: AgentRxiv: Towards Collaborative Autonomous Research
records.summary: Lets agent laboratories publish and retrieve reports through a shared preprint server, allowing later research runs to build on earlier findings. Experiments on reasoning and prompting methods compare shared research against isolated agents. The measured gains concern benchmark-solving strategies, not a demonstrated open scientific community across disciplines.

records.name: BixBench
records.summary: Evaluates bioinformatics agents on more than 50 practical analysis scenarios with nearly 300 associated questions. Tasks require exploring biological datasets, performing multistep analyses, and interpreting results. Open-answer and multiple-choice settings test different behaviors; correctness on these prepared analyses should not be presented as validation of new biological mechanisms or experimental discoveries.

records.name: Google Co-Scientist
records.summary: A Gemini-based system in which agents generate, critique, rank, and refine scientific hypotheses in collaboration with researchers. Google describes biological case studies and an experimental Hypothesis Generation access route. This is a hosted research partner focused on hypothesis development; a general open-source implementation of Google's system was not confirmed.

records.name: Agent Laboratory
records.summary: Organizes specialist agents around literature review, planning, experimentation, and reporting for a researcher-supplied idea. The open implementation supports human feedback during the workflow and machine-learning experimentation. It provides a concrete research-assistant baseline; the quality and efficiency claims in its paper should be interpreted within the evaluated tasks and model configurations.

records.name: Agent Laboratory: Using LLM Agents as Research Assistants
records.summary: Takes a human research idea through literature review, experimentation, and report writing, producing code and a manuscript while allowing feedback at each stage. Comparisons across models and a researcher study report benefits from human guidance. The results support supervised research assistance within the tested machine-learning workflows.

records.name: AIDE
records.summary: Searches over executable machine-learning solutions by repeatedly drafting, debugging, evaluating, and improving code against a specified metric. The public reference implementation includes configuration and search-tree inspection utilities. It is a reusable experiment-search component and benchmark baseline, with results bounded by evaluator quality, data access, and safeguards against exploiting the evaluation setup.

records.name: Biomni
records.summary: A biomedical research agent that combines retrieval-guided planning with executable code and a broad scientific software environment. Its repository exposes the agent, environment setup, tutorials, and supported research workflows. It is useful for investigating tool-rich biological analysis; biomedical task demonstrations do not establish clinical safety or reliability across all research domains.

records.name: OpenEvolve
records.summary: An open community implementation inspired by AlphaEvolve that evolves programs using language models, evaluator feedback, and population-based search. It includes examples for mathematical optimization, scientific computing, and kernel improvement. The repository is independently maintained rather than Google's original system, and its reported improvements should be checked against the corresponding evaluator and hardware conditions.

records.name: R&D-Agent
records.summary: Separates research proposal generation from development and evaluation, then iterates using experimental feedback. Microsoft's public project includes data-science, model-development, and quantitative-finance scenarios. It offers a practical architecture for automating repeated implementation work; success in an included scenario does not establish broad scientific discovery ability or transfer to unrelated domains.

records.name: ShinkaEvolve
records.summary: Combines language-model program mutations with evolutionary search, solution archives, and evaluation feedback to improve algorithms. The public framework supports local or cluster evaluation and tasks with executable verifiers. It is suited to measurable algorithm discovery, with scientific conclusions limited by what the verifier and optimization objective actually test.

records.name: ToolUniverse
records.summary: Provides a common interface for scientific tools, datasets, models, and APIs so language-model agents can discover and invoke external capabilities. The public project offers a Python SDK and agent integrations. It supplies infrastructure for building scientific assistants; available tool connectors do not by themselves establish reliable tool selection, valid analyses, or experimental reproducibility.

records.name: Virtual Lab
records.summary: Structures collaboration between a human researcher and specialist language-model agents through team and individual meetings. The public code includes the nanobody-design application accompanying a Nature study with experimental validation. This supplies a grounded example of collaborative scientific discovery, while the biological evidence applies to that specific campaign rather than unrestricted autonomous laboratory work.

records.name: Autonomous LLM-driven research from data to human-verifiable research papers
records.summary: Guides agents from annotated data through hypotheses, analysis code, results, and a manuscript while tracing information backward to its sources. The study reports stronger reliability for simpler goals and limited novelty, with human co-piloting increasingly important as complexity rises. Traceability is a central design feature rather than an afterthought.

records.name: RE-Bench
records.summary: Compares agents with human experts on seven open-ended machine-learning research engineering environments, including optimization tasks with executable scoring functions. Its human-attempt data and multiple time budgets make resource assumptions visible. Results concern bounded AI research engineering, and rankings can change with time allowance; they do not establish general scientific autonomy.

records.name: CycleResearcher: Improving Automated Research via Automated Review
records.summary: Trains research-writing and reviewing models in a feedback cycle using research and peer-review datasets. Generated papers are refined through simulated review, with evaluations of score prediction and manuscript ratings. Those simulated ratings measure an important writing-and-review capability, but should not be interpreted as independently executed experiments or scientific discoveries.

records.name: MLE-bench
records.summary: Packages 75 Kaggle competitions to assess dataset preparation, model training, and iterative experimentation, with historical leaderboard thresholds as reference points. Useful for engineering-focused research agents and resource-scaling studies. A competition medal measures predictive performance under a particular setup; it is not evidence of novel hypotheses or scientific validity beyond that task.

records.name: MOOSE-Chem: Large Language Models for Rediscovering Unseen Chemistry Scientific Hypotheses
records.summary: Decomposes hypothesis discovery into retrieving inspirations, composing hypotheses, and ranking them. A chemist-annotated benchmark uses papers published after the evaluated model's stated training cutoff to test rediscovery. Similarity to withheld published hypotheses measures a useful capability, but does not establish prospective novelty or successful laboratory realization.

records.name: ScienceAgentBench
records.summary: Contains 102 expert-validated tasks derived from 44 publications across four disciplines. Each task requires a self-contained Python program, assessed through code, execution outputs, and costs. The benchmark deliberately tests individual data-driven research steps, providing a stronger basis for bounded capability claims than treating generated manuscripts as evidence of complete scientific discovery.

records.name: Scideator: Human-LLM Compound System for Scientific Ideation through Facet Recombination and Novelty Evaluation
records.summary: Extracts purpose, mechanism, and evaluation facets from papers, lets researchers recombine them, and retrieves related work to assess originality. The updated paper reports creativity-support benefits and novelty-checking ablations. Its contribution is an interactive ideation process, with user judgments and retrieval quality distinct from validating a finished scientific result.

records.name: CORE-Bench
records.summary: Measures computational reproducibility using supplied code and data: 270 tasks from 90 papers across computer science, social science, and medicine, with three difficulty levels. Agents must recover results and answer questions about them. Re-running artifacts does not validate the underlying scientific claims; the 2026 follow-up introduces v1.1 and out-of-distribution tasks after auditing shortcuts.

records.name: PaperQA2
records.summary: An agentic retrieval system for answering scientific questions with cited evidence from documents. It combines paper search, metadata collection, contextual evidence summaries, and iterative answer generation, with a public Python package and command-line interface. The research reports strong literature-task performance; those results concern particular evaluations rather than guaranteed factual correctness for every answer.

records.name: SciAgents: Automating scientific discovery through multi-agent intelligent graph reasoning
records.summary: Combines ontological knowledge graphs, retrieval tools, and collaborating language-model agents to propose and critique interdisciplinary hypotheses. Biologically inspired materials case studies illustrate connections between concepts and proposed mechanisms. The primary evidence is hypothesis-generation and reasoning case studies, which should be separated from laboratory verification of resulting material designs.

records.name: Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with 100+ NLP Researchers
records.summary: Uses blinded comparisons between researcher-written and agent-generated NLP ideas, involving more than one hundred researchers. AI ideas receive higher novelty judgments but weaker feasibility judgments, while self-evaluation and diversity remain problematic. The experiment evaluates perceived idea quality, not whether executing those ideas yields stronger scientific discoveries.

records.name: The AI Scientist: Towards Fully Automated Open-Ended Scientific Discovery
records.summary: Connects idea generation, code editing, experiments, visualization, manuscript drafting, and automated reviewing around human-provided research templates. Demonstrations cover diffusion models, language models, and learning dynamics. Paper-quality claims rely substantially on an automated reviewer, and the template dependence bounds the extent of open-ended autonomy demonstrated.

records.name: SciCode
records.summary: Uses 80 scientist-authored research coding problems, decomposed into 338 subproblems across 16 subfields, to test scientific knowledge and executable implementation. Report main-problem and subproblem accuracy separately, including whether background information was supplied. This assesses specified computational tasks; the later SciCode-Verified audit also makes benchmark version and test defects relevant to comparisons.

records.name: LAB-Bench
records.summary: Provides more than 2,400 multiple-choice questions targeting practical biology-research capabilities, including literature reasoning, figure interpretation, database navigation, and sequence manipulation. Expert comparisons help contextualize performance on research-adjacent tasks. These are bounded question-answer evaluations, so high scores alone do not demonstrate reliable laboratory execution, end-to-end biological research, or novel experimental validation.

records.name: DiscoveryBench
records.summary: Tests hypothesis discovery from supplied datasets, metadata, and natural-language goals using 264 literature-derived tasks across six domains, plus 903 synthetic tasks. Facet-based evaluation separates aspects of a proposed finding. The target is recovering supported relationships within provided data, with synthetic and real tasks reported separately, rather than discovering unrestricted new scientific knowledge.

records.name: BioDiscoveryAgent: An AI Agent for Designing Genetic Perturbation Experiments
records.summary: Selects genetic perturbations using language-model knowledge, literature search, code analysis, and critique, then updates proposals from experimental outcomes. Evaluation across perturbation datasets compares it with Bayesian optimization and random selection. The evidence concerns efficient experiment selection in the tested settings rather than autonomous validation of arbitrary biological mechanisms.

records.name: ChemCrow: Augmenting large language models with chemistry tools
records.summary: Augments a language model with expert-designed chemistry tools for synthesis, molecular tasks, and materials design. The work includes executed synthesis examples and expert assessment. Its preprint also highlights weaknesses in using a language model to judge chemical correctness, underscoring why tool execution and independent expert evaluation matter.

records.name: ResearchAgent: Iterative Research Idea Generation over Scientific Literature with Large Language Models
records.summary: Expands a seed paper through an academic graph and a concept store, then iteratively refines proposed problems, methods, and experimental designs using reviewing agents. Human and model evaluations cover multiple disciplines. The demonstrated output is a research proposal; executing the experiments and validating its scientific claims remain separate tasks.

records.name: Docling
records.summary: Converts PDFs and other documents into structured representations for retrieval and downstream analysis, including layout-aware extraction and handling of tables and figures. Its open implementation supports research-document ingestion. It is an enabling component rather than a scientist agent; extraction quality should be checked before treating parsed tables, formulas, or reading order as reliable evidence.

records.name: MLAgentBench
records.summary: Evaluates agents that read and modify files, run experiments, and inspect results across 13 machine-learning tasks, from CIFAR-10 improvement to BabyLM. Task success exposes planning and experimentation failures within supplied problems; it does not measure autonomous selection of important research questions or independently validated scientific discoveries.

records.name: OpenScholar
records.summary: Pairs scientific retrieval with a language model trained to synthesize evidence and attach supporting citations. The authors provide implementation resources, models, data, and scientific question-answering evaluations, with a later Nature publication. It is a foundation for literature-grounded assistants; retrieval coverage and citation quality remain properties to evaluate for each downstream corpus and task.

records.name: STORM / Co-STORM
records.summary: Builds sourced topic outlines and long-form articles by combining retrieval with questions from multiple perspectives. Co-STORM adds collaborative discussion and a shared concept map so users can steer exploration. The official implementation is useful for research preparation and knowledge curation; its authors explicitly note that generated articles often require substantial editing.

records.name: The AI Scientist
records.summary: Implements a template-based loop for proposing ideas, changing experimental code, running machine-learning experiments, and drafting papers with an automated reviewer. The repository provides executable workflows and example outputs. Its structured starting templates make it a useful baseline for research automation, while generated manuscripts still require inspection of results, citations, and methodological claims.

records.name: Coscientist: Autonomous chemical research with large language models
records.summary: Connects language-model planning to web and documentation search, code execution, and experimental equipment. Demonstrations include chemical synthesis planning and reaction optimization, illustrating how tool access can turn reasoning into physical experiments. The work operates within a configured laboratory and selected tasks, with human setup and oversight remaining important.

records.name: FunSearch: Mathematical discoveries from program search with large language models
records.summary: Pairs a language model with an evaluator and an evolving database of programs, searching for code that constructs strong solutions. The paper reports new cap-set constructions and improved bin-packing heuristics. Its successes depend on explicit evaluators and problem specifications, making the verification mechanism central to its scientific relevance.

records.name: GPT Researcher
records.summary: A configurable research agent that decomposes questions, gathers evidence from web or local sources, and assembles cited reports. It exposes a package, interfaces, and multi-agent or recursive research workflows. It is useful as a general research component, but its project-level claims should not be confused with scientific novelty or independently validated literature-review completeness.

records.name: SciMON: Scientific Inspiration Machines Optimized for Novelty
records.summary: Retrieves scientific inspirations and iteratively revises proposed ideas by comparing them with prior literature. Its contextual idea-generation setting goes beyond predicting links between concepts. Human-oriented evaluations show improvements over baseline generation while also exposing limited technical depth and novelty, making it useful for studying ideation quality rather than experimental discovery.

records.name: Coscientist
records.summary: Connects language models with literature and documentation search, code execution, and laboratory automation for chemistry tasks. The Nature study demonstrates planning and execution across several experimental settings. The public repository contains supporting data and a simplified implementation, with commercial-use restrictions; it should not be described as a complete unrestricted release of the original laboratory system.

records.name: ASReview LAB
records.summary: Uses active learning to prioritize records during systematic literature screening while preserving human inclusion decisions. It provides a screening interface, simulation tools, label management, and exportable review state. This is a complementary evidence-selection tool rather than a generative scientist; screening completeness depends on the review protocol, labels, and stopping decision.

records.name: The Automation of Science (Robot Scientist Adam)
records.summary: Combines hypothesis generation, automated laboratory experiments, and a logical record of the research process to study yeast functional genomics. The authors report manual confirmation of Adam's conclusions. This pre-LLM example grounds modern autonomy discussions in a closed experimental loop and explicit provenance within a constrained biological problem.
